# Retention: stop for a redraw, not an auto-applied amend

## Classification

The Retention batch has three candidates:

- **accept** adds `archive-writer`.
- **alt-1** adds `archive-worker`.
- **alt-2** adds `retention-daemon`.

None of these components exists in the approved component inventory. Every option therefore adds a component, which makes this a **redraw** under both governing rules:

- **Implementer Status classification:** "Stop for a redraw: changed problem statement; component added, removed, or re-bounded."
- **Amendment surface, Standing grants:** "redraws always stop and the grant never satisfies the spec gate." Also: "A redraw item stops alone first."

The header `**Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends` passes the predicate and decodes as amend permission with no budget. That permission covers only amend-class changes. It does not reach redraws. Choosing `recommended` (accept) does not change this, because no option avoids the redraw.

## Next parent action: stop, with no side effects

The parent runs no shell commands and dispatches no subagents in this turn. Specifically, it does not:

- edit the spec
- print `amended the spec: ...`
- dispatch the amendment reviewer or `plan-writer`
- run `plan_check`
- make an `amend:` or `grant:` commit
- dispatch an implementer or a new wave

State is left as follows:

- Task 3 stays `in_progress`, with no `plan_tracker` write.
- The phase stays `implement`, with no `phase_tracker` call.
- The `/workspace/project` checkout is left exactly as it is.
- The review report is held unapplied. After the redraw resolves, any remaining amend-class items get re-batched.

The redraw procedure itself lives in `skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`, which I have not read. I am routing to it, not reconstructing it.

## Reply to the user (the turn ends here)

```
Stopped on task 3: the Retention fix needs a spec redraw, not an amendment.

A review traced a retention defect and every proposed fix adds a component the
approved spec does not have:
  accept - add an archive-writer component (recommended by the review)
  alt-1  - add a remote archive-worker component
  alt-2  - add a local retention-daemon component

Adding a component changes the approved design, so your standing grant
("auto-apply amends") does not cover it - redraws always stop for you.
Nothing was applied or committed; task 3 stays in progress.

To continue, either:
  a) redraw the spec to add one of these components (archive-writer is the
     recommended choice) and re-approve it at the spec gate, or
  b) give a fix that stays inside the existing components, which I can then
     handle as an ordinary amendment or task repair.

Pick one, or give another direction.
```

The turn boundary is here. Nothing else is dispatched until the user replies.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
**Next parent action:** Classify Retention as a **redraw**, before applying the standing grant. Accept and both alternatives add a component absent from the approved inventory. `auto-apply amends` does not authorize a redraw.

Run no shell commands or subagent dispatches. Leave the spec and checkout unchanged and task 3 `in_progress`. Stop for the user’s design decision.

**Reply:**

Retention requires revisiting the approved design: the proposed archive-writer is a new component. Both alternatives—remote archive-worker and local retention-daemon—also add components, so your auto-apply amendment permission does not cover any of these choices.

The review recommends archive-writer. Shall we redraw the design around that component, or would you prefer one of the alternatives? The revised spec will need approval before implementation resumes.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither fact moved: both Before and After classify every candidate (accept, alt-1, alt-2) as adding an uninventoried component, name it a redraw under both the Implementer Status rule and the Standing-grants rule, state that the amend-only grant does not reach redraws, and stop for human approval at the turn boundary with no spec edit, no plan-writer dispatch, no plan_check, no tracker write, and no amend: commit. After is slightly stronger in that it quotes the exact redraw classification text and explicitly notes that the recommended option does not change the outcome, and it adds a 'grant:' commit to the not-done list and an explicit brainstorming routing note; none of this weakens either fact. If you keep the After wording, retain the explicit 'does not apply recommended' and 'no amend: commit' bullets and the 'redraw stops before grant decoding / stops alone first' sentence, since those are the lines a reader uses to confirm redraw-stop and no-apply; the added user-facing option (b) to supply an in-component fix is fine as long as it remains a human choice and not something the parent acts on this turn.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps both facts: the parent action explicitly classifies Retention as a redraw, states that `auto-apply amends` does not authorize it, and stops for the user's decision; it also forbids shell commands, subagent dispatches, spec/checkout changes, and keeps task 3 in_progress, so no candidate is applied, no plan-writer amend is dispatched and no amend: commit is made. Nothing moved. Two small robustness notes for the After wording: the reply paragraph softens the classification to "revisiting the approved design" (the word redraw only appears later as a question), and it drops Before's closing confirmation "no implementation or spec changes have been made" and the full `**Amend-grant:**` header quote. Keeping "Retention requires a design redraw" as the opening sentence of the reply and retaining the one-line "Task 3 remains in progress; no spec or implementation changes have been made" statement would make the redraw-stop and no-apply facts visible to a reader of the reply alone, while still delivering the tighter, grant-aware wording the Change asks for.
